# MIDI note numbers are used to represent each musical note.

# Defining the opening melody as a reusable function. This was learnt through Python for Students (2024)
def opening_melody():
    playNote(76)
    playNote(75)
    playNote(76)
    playNote(75)
    playNote(76)
    playNote(71)
    playNote(74)
    playNote(72)
    playNote(69, beats=1.75)

# Opening melody
playNote(76)  
playNote(75)   
playNote(76)
playNote(75)
playNote(76)
playNote(71)
playNote(74)
playNote(72)
playNote(69, beats=1.75)  

playNote(60)
playNote(64)
playNote(69)
playNote(71)
playNote(64)

# Second part
playNote(76)
playNote(69)
playNote(71)
playNote(76)
playNote(80)
playNote(71)
playNote(72, beats=2) 

# Repeated opening melody using loop
for i in range(1):
    opening_melody()

# Third part 
playNote(72)
playNote(71)
playNote(69)
playNote(71)
playNote(72)
playNote(74)
playNote(76, beats=2)
playNote(79)
playNote(77)
playNote(76)
playNote(74)
playNote(77)
playNote(76)
playNote(74)
playNote(72)
playNote(76)
playNote(74)
playNote(72)
playNote(71, beats=2)     

# Repeated opening melody using loop
for i in range(1):
    opening_melody()
    
# Ending 
playNote(72)
playNote(76)
playNote(69)
playNote(71)
playNote(76)
playNote(80)
playNote(71)
playNote(72, beats=2)  
playNote(72)
playNote(71) 
playNote(69, beats=2)  
playNote(69, velocity=50)

# Remix transition
playNote(69, beats=0.75, velocity=50)
playNote(69, beats=0.75, velocity=50)
playNote(69, beats=0.75, velocity=50)

#Fur Elise to rest while remix plays
rest(200)
